headline: Trump intensifies push to reshape election rules as Supreme Court curbs Voting Rights Act ahead of 2026 midterms
consensus: Multiple outlets report that President Trump is moving aggressively to alter federal election rules and structures ahead of the 2026 midterms, even as the Supreme Court has narrowed a key Voting Rights Act protection and early special-election results raise questions about Republican prospects.

sections.subheading: Trump's Push to Reshape Election Rules

sentences.text: In a prime-time address, President Trump laid out his priorities for the coming year, with commentators noting several key takeaways from the speech.
With time running out before the midterms, Trump has dug in on efforts to change election rules.
He has been urged by allies to declare a national emergency to seize greater executive power over elections, and has since made such a declaration, leaving Republican allies scrambling to respond.
Trump has remained defiant even in the face of rare resistance from congressional Republicans.
He also fired members of a bipartisan federal elections commission.
A voting bill that Trump has said will secure electoral victory could instead backfire on Republicans, according to analysis.

sections.subheading: Supreme Court Narrows the Voting Rights Act

sentences.text: The Supreme Court limited a key provision of the landmark Voting Rights Act.
PBS characterized the ruling as weakening the civil rights-era law in a way that aids Republican efforts to control the House.
In response, Black members of Congress said they are focusing on generating 'massive voter turnout' after the law was gutted.

sections.subheading: Supreme Court Narrows the Voting Rights Act

sentences.text: The Washington Post described the same ruling more narrowly as limiting a key provision of the Voting Rights Act, without framing it explicitly in terms of partisan advantage.
With midterm elections now nine months away, analysts are assessing the shifting political terrain.
Republican wins on redistricting and election maps have given Democrats a steeper climb toward retaking control of Congress.
A Republican loss in Trump's own Mar-a-Lago congressional district has been read as a signal about midterm dynamics.
The White House has told House Republicans to avoid talking about mass deportation ahead of the midterms.
Separately, two wealthy Democratic donors who were once friends are now spending millions of dollars attacking each other.
